To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present an attentive RNN model that keeps track of party states in conversations, which outperforms the current state of the art on two different datasets.

(i) we introduce a new model, DialogueRNN, that keeps track of individual party states and uses it to classify the emotion of each utterance; (ii) our model outperforms state of the art methods on two different datasets; and (iii) we show that the model learns to identify the speaker and adapts to his/her emotion style.

(i) a simple RNN architecture can achieve state-of-the-art results in conversation emotion detection, (ii) the model can learn to track the state of the parties in the dialog and (iii) the model can achieve state-ofthe-art results on two datasets, one of which is a new one we release as part of this work.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of detecting emotions from conversations, and we propose a new approach that is based on an attentive RNN that keeps track of both the speaker and the conversation context.
